prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Sentinel Vale: ground-only land/coastal/cryosphere imagery; predictable latency,documented quality,retained external interfaces. Elements: Mission Control Center(Bluebell/local voice)—safety/pass/anomaly supervision,commands,schedules,routing; Flight Dynamics Facility(Mistral/legacy logs)—navigation/maneuvers,pre-release visibility/pointing products; Mission Planning System—demand/constraints→plans; receives contact booking requests(service,antenna,elevation,volume,priority); Command Validation Gateway—mandatory pre-uplink checks; Network Control System(Lantern)—authoritative circuits/routing/allocations/readiness/contact records; sends Bluebell pre-pass antenna status,link configuration,timing references,routing readiness; Ground Network Manager(Juniper/rosters)—antenna assignments,availability/conflicts/maintenance/staffing/site coordination; issues Antenna Deicing Notice,pins maintenance-critical pre-acquisition tasks; Orbit Determination Engine—tracking→orbit/state updates,visibility/maneuver/pointing basis,qualified-pass Doppler Residual Report; Telemetry Ingest Service—real-time frames/contact/data-flow indicators→operations/engineering/processing; validates framing/time continuity,records metadata,distinguishes gaps/interruptions; produces post-contact Pass Replay Packet for engineering reconstruction. Payload Processing Facility(Forgehouse/console discussions/shift logs)—processing/calibration/distribution; Primary Processing Cluster(nominal),Backup Processing Cluster(controlled failover); Product Quality Service—pre-distribution checks; Long Term Archive—authoritative data/products/evidence; User Services Portal—search/orders/status/support. Actors: Spacecraft Operations Team—safety/authorization,Bluebell-console monitoring(mode,power,thermal,attitude,command counters,storage,fault protection); console lead—declares pass status,authorizes planned commands through Gateway,pauses unexpected configurations; telemetry engineer—quality/loss/latency/continuity,advises command confidence; spacecraft systems engineer—health/flight-rule compliance,anomaly context. Flight Dynamics Team—contact tracking/validated timestamps→Mistral orbit assessment; separates clock bias/tracking error. Payload Calibration Team—quality. Cybersecurity Desk—monitoring/escalation,Security Exception Ticket for temporary baseline deviations. Local station teams—configuration/frequencies/time/interlocks/logs; station operators→Bluebell constraints. North S-Band Antenna(nominal),South S-Band Antenna(procedure-compatible alternate): commands/low-rate telemetry→Bluebell via protected

New part:
S093: The Mission Control Center coordinates with the Payload Processing Facility when instrument mode changes, data downlink priorities, or reception gaps could affect downstream processing.
S094: The Payload Calibration Team sends the Calibration Patch Bundle after calibration analysis identifies an approved update for payload processing behavior.
S095: Subsystem specialists are not expected to staff every live contact, but they must be reachable during planned critical activities and whenever a console operator declares an off-nominal condition.
S096: Escalation from the Mission Control Center begins with the console lead, moves to the responsible discipline lead, and then reaches mission management when the condition threatens spacecraft safety, contact continuity, or recovery schedule.
S097: The Spacecraft Operations Team and Flight Dynamics Team coordinate closely before orbit-control activities so that command timing, attitude constraints, tracking expectations, and post-burn assessment steps remain consistent.
S098: When telemetry indicates a possible onboard fault, operators preserve the command state, avoid discretionary commanding, and request specialist review before changing spacecraft configuration.
S099: The Mission Planning System receives operational constraints from mission control after anomalies, station outages, or spacecraft configuration changes require adjustment of future contacts or payload activities.
S100: At the end of each shift, the Mission Control Center records unresolved actions, open engineering questions, and expected specialist responses so that the next operations crew can maintain continuity without relying on informal handover.
S101: Mission planning begins when observation requests arrive through the User Services Portal or from internal operations channels at the Mission Control Center.
S102: The Mission Planning System, also called Cedar in this section, is the authoritative tool for assembling candidate observation timelines and associated ground contact activities.
S103: Each request is checked for requester authority, target definition, time sensitivity, acquisition mode, expected data volume, and any handling restrictions before it is admitted to the planning pool.
S104: The User Services Portal records the request state so that external users can distinguish accepted requests from those still awaiting technical review.
S105: The Spacecraft Operations Team reviews late operational requests when they affect spacecraft attitude, thermal margin, stored command capacity, or contact preparation.
S106: The Flight Dynamics Facility provides orbit predictions and visibility assumptions that the planning cycle uses to determine feasible imaging windows and ground contacts.
S107: The Mission Planning System combines request priority, instrument availability, contact opportunities, onboard storage margin, and downlink capacity into a draft activity schedule.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
